gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 'HYROX race mode' means two different things: on the sub-$150 picks (Amazfit Bip 6 $79.99, Active 2 $99.99) you change every run/station segment yourself and Zepp's roadmap gives them no automatic transitions, while the Amazfit Bip Max at the same $99.99 has HYROX Race/PFT/Training and is on the roadmap for automatic transitions in December 2026 (COROS PACE 3 already has auto-transition but costs $199).
standout_why: Of the pages ChatGPT got, roxskin.io (cited in one chat) has part of this. It says the Active 2 uses manual segment changes, that COROS Hybrid Fitness has auto or manual transitions, and that the Bip 6 is missing from Amazfit's auto-transition rollout list. It never mentions the Bip Max, gives no prices that line manual and auto up against a $150 limit, and gives no dates. Our current page (dealectric.com) labels all three Amazfit watches 'HYROX Race, built in' and doesn't separate manual from auto. Its PACE 3 cell says 'Dual-frequency, 38 h', but COROS's page ties the 38 h to standard GPS. None of the ChatGPT answers mention the Bip Max or the difference between manual and automatic transitions. I couldn't open wearablebeat.com (403) or roxgrit.com (certificate error), so I couldn't compare against them.
decides: The pick needs a footnote and possibly a different alternative. The Bip 6 and Active 2 remain the cheapest watches whose HYROX mode works on stock firmware today, but you advance each segment yourself. For the same $99.99 as the Active 2, the Bip Max adds HYROX PFT/Training modes and a dated (secondhand) path to automatic transitions. The trade-off is weight: 52.6 g against 29.5 g for the Active 2 on our current page. No watch under $150 ships automatic HYROX transitions today. The only sourced one is the PACE 3 at $199. The Active 2 Square at $149.99 has the same HYROX race mode as the Round for $50 more, so the Round stays the better buy.
